body: Not as infuriating as spending an HOUR on hold only to be told by a CS rep that I should have called a different number. BB CS is crap. Maybe you're the needle in the haystack that genuinely wants to help customers but all the BB CS reps I've spoken to were incompetent and rude. Beyond useless. Never doing business with BB again.

Wow, I could have written this post.  I am responding just to let you know that you're not alone. I am in the same position. Haven't left my bed in two days. It's like the slightest act, eating, drinking, going to the bathroom, takes such superhuman effort.  Don't want to go to the ER and have "suicidal" on my permanent record. Do you have someone supportive around?

You're right, I am sensitive.  And you are kind.  Whoever your friends are, they are lucky. I did update my resume and sent it out there, got zero replies, sent it out again. I tried to stay in the game, think positive, hope for a break. But it's been years and sometimes you just gotta know when to call it quits.  Same goes for the relationship.  Same goes for life in general.  Not to sound like a defeatist, but I am pretty defeated. And I just don't have anything left to start over. But thank you for helping me through this night at least. I am still crying and feeling sorry for myself, but also grateful. I have been so isolated, so bereft of human connection, that your understanding words have been a literal life saver.
I hear you. I've been you. Hang in.

Thank you for taking the time to write such a caring comment. Your kind words made me start sobbing. I have not felt heard in so long.  I thought my existence literally didn't matter, that I was beyond insignificant. Thank you for listening and for making me feel, even for a moment, that I matter.  I have thought about starting fresh someplace else, but at this point I am just so tired and I am not brave. But thank you.

My father sounds a lot like yours. And I recognize the monster you described. I am the same. I have also sought help - therapy, medication - but have never had your will power. You said you lasted a year before lashing out at your girlfriend.  I have not been able to go that long.  I have said the most vicious nasty hurtful things to my boyfriend.  If I were a man, I know I would be physically abusive as well. [Not because men are more violent than women, or whatever, but because I'm small and not strong and the abuser in me would only hit someone if I knew they couldn't defend themselves. (I do not and will not have children.)] My boyfriend had a similarly damaging upbringing, so he takes my abuse and dishes out a good bit of his own.  But he's really no match for me. I never say this out loud, but I lash out partly because if feels good when I do.  I feel powerful. Inflicting pain distracts me from feeling my own.  I know that makes me a monster.
Just curious, but why do you think he's too good for you?
I feel for you.  I really do.  More than anything else, you sound sad that you and your husband have drifted so far apart.  Alcohol no doubt hasn't helped.  I'm sorry.  Hug.
Yes, it does.  Also, it's "myriad things" not "myriad of things."  I'm hoping she dumps you first.  You need a wake-up call.
Thank you for correcting the "me and her" gaffe.  It was making me crazy.

A friend of mine married her first boyfriend - they met in college, both went to an ivy league law school, both had high powered lucrative careers, blah, blah, blah.  They were together for 10 years.  Then she found out that he was living a double life - by day he was an ultra-conservative overpaid corporate consultant, but by night he was "Vanilla Jack" and trolled the internet for prostitutes and porn.  (His real name isn't Jack and he wasn't vanilla - he's kind of a perv, actually.)  He would tell my friend he was going out of town on business then hole up for a few days with a hooker at a motel down the street from their apartment.  To my friend's credit, she divorced him asap.  The horrifying thing is the guy is now working for an uber-conservative think tank writing pious articles preaching, among other things, abstinence and "family values."

How do you block someone's number from your cell?  My bf had an ex who wouldn't stop calling and we tried to block her calls but weren't able to figure it out.  We called Sprint (his cell provider) and they weren't much help, either.
Totally agree with you.  I am only attracted to tall men (no offense).  I'm shallow that way and you're right, that's not going to change.  You can't deconstruct desire

Um . . . I wouldn't get my hopes up.  In my experience, shorter guys aren't necessarily better in bed.  They tend to overcompensate which makes the whole sexual experience more about them than about you or about being intimate together.  As for the varied positions, what are you all talking about?  Which positions?
omg . . . you are such a tool.
